<h3>
<span lang="sr">
Номинатив
</span>

Nominative
</em>
</h3>

NOM
</span>

<p class="q">
<strong lang="sr">
ко? / шта?
</strong>
— who, what.
</p>
</header>
</div>

</span>
</span>

<span class="ending-unit">
<span class="eu-gender" data-gender="f">

</span>

<article class="case-row" data-tone="ins" id="case-6">
<div class="case-cell case-cell-head">
<header class="case-head">
<div class="case-head-title">
<h3>
<span lang="sr">
Инструментал
</span>
<em>
Instrumental
</em>
</h3>
<span class="case-tag">
INS
</span>
</div>

### popover [data-note-trigger]|[["data-case-idx","0"],["data-note-id","sib-i"],["data-note-trigger",null]]
<article class="note-pop">
<h4 class="note-title">
<i lang="sr">
к, г, х
</i>
soften before
<i lang="sr">
-и
</i>
</h4>
<p class="note-body">
These three hard consonants don't sit comfortably next to a bright
<i lang="sr">
-и
</i>
. They shift to softer cousins —
<i lang="sr">
ц, з, с
</i>
— that match the vowel better.
</p>
<ul class="note-pairs">
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
јуна
<span class="lit">
к
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
јуна
<span class="lit">
ци
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
јези
<span class="lit">
к
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
јези
<span class="lit">
ци
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
мона
<span class="lit">
х
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
мона
<span class="lit">
си
</span>
</span>
</li>
</ul>
</article>
### popover [data-note-trigger]|[["data-case-idx","2"],["data-note-id","sib-i"],["data-note-trigger",null]]
<article class="note-pop">
<h4 class="note-title">
<i lang="sr">
к, г, х
</i>
soften before the
<i lang="sr">
-и
</i>
ending
</h4>
<p class="note-body">
When the feminine singular ending
<i lang="sr">
-и
</i>
lands on a stem ending in
<i lang="sr">
к
</i>
,
<i lang="sr">
г
</i>
, or
<i lang="sr">
х
</i>
, those hard consonants shift to
<i lang="sr">
ц, з, с
</i>
— softer sounds that sit better next to the
<i lang="sr">
-и
</i>
.
</p>
<ul class="note-pairs">
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
књи
<span class="lit">
га
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
књи
<span class="lit">
зи
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
ру
<span class="lit">
ка
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
ру
<span class="lit">
ци
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
Амери
<span class="lit">
ка
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
Амери
<span class="lit">
ци
</span>
</span>
</li>
</ul>

### popover [data-note-trigger]|[["data-case-idx","3"],["data-note-id","animacy"],["data-note-trigger",null]]
<article class="note-pop">
<h4 class="note-title">
Living things vs everything else
</h4>
<p class="note-body">
In the masculine singular only, the accusative splits by whether the noun is alive. Living things (people, animals) take
<i lang="sr">
-а
</i>
— the same shape as the genitive. Inanimate things take
<i lang="sr">
-∅
</i>
— the nominative form, unchanged. So you reuse two endings you already know.
</p>
<ul class="note-pairs">
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
пилот
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
пилот
<span class="lit">
а
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
град
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
град
</span>
</li>
</ul>
</article>
### popover [data-note-trigger]|[["data-case-idx","4"],["data-note-id","palatal"],["data-note-trigger",null]]
<article class="note-pop">
<h4 class="note-title">
<i lang="sr">
к, г, х
</i>
turn into
<i lang="sr">
ч, ж, ш
</i>
when calling out
</h4>
<p class="note-body">
When you address someone whose word ends in
<i lang="sr">
к
</i>
,
<i lang="sr">
г
</i>
, or
<i lang="sr">
х
</i>
, those consonants shift to their soft cousins —
<i lang="sr">
ч, ж, ш
</i>
— before the
<i lang="sr">
-е
</i>
ending. The hard sounds soften because you're calling, not stating.
</p>
<ul class="note-pairs">
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
јуна
<span class="lit">
к
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
јуна
<span class="lit">
че
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
Бо
<span class="lit">
г
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
Бо
<span class="lit">
же
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
ду
<span class="lit">
х
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
ду
<span class="lit">
ше
</span>
</span>
</li>
</ul>
</article>
### popover [data-note-trigger]|[["data-case-idx","4"],["data-note-id","soft"],["data-note-trigger",null]]
<article class="note-pop">
<h4 class="note-title">
After soft consonants, use
<i lang="sr">
-у
</i>
instead of
<i lang="sr">
-е
</i>
</h4>
<p class="note-body">
If the word already ends in a soft consonant —
<i lang="sr">
ц, ћ, ч, ђ, џ, ј, љ, њ, ш, ж
</i>
— adding a soft
<i lang="sr">
-е
</i>
on top would feel doubled. The ending switches to
<i lang="sr">
-у
</i>
instead.
</p>
<ul class="note-pairs">
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
пријатељ
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
пријатељ
<span class="lit">
у
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
младић
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
младић
<span class="lit">
у
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
муж
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
муж
<span class="lit">
у
</span>
</span>
</li>
</ul>
</article>
### popover [data-note-trigger]|[["data-case-idx","4"],["data-note-id","vok-f-name"],["data-note-trigger",null]]
<article class="note-pop">
<h4 class="note-title">
Names usually keep their
<i lang="sr">
-а
</i>
</h4>
<p class="note-body">
Common nouns take
<i lang="sr">
-о
</i>
. Personal names normally stay unchanged when you call them, and diminutives in
<i lang="sr">
-ица
</i>
switch to
<i lang="sr">
-е
</i>
. Putting
<i lang="sr">
-о
</i>
on a name sounds formal or folkloric.
</p>
<ul class="note-pairs">
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
жен
<span class="lit">
а
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
жен
<span class="lit">
о
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
Марија
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
Марија
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
сестриц
<span class="lit">
а
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
сестриц
<span class="lit">
е
</span>
</span>
</li>
</ul>
</article>
### popover [data-note-trigger]|[["data-case-idx","5"],["data-note-id","soft-em"],["data-note-trigger",null]]
<article class="note-pop">
<h4 class="note-title">
After soft consonants,
<i lang="sr">
-ом
</i>
becomes
<i lang="sr">
-ем
</i>
</h4>
<p class="note-body">
The round
<i lang="sr">
-ом
</i>
feels heavy when it follows a soft consonant (
<i lang="sr">
ц, ћ, ч, ђ, џ, ј, љ, њ, ш, ж
</i>
). It thins to
<i lang="sr">
-ем
</i>
so the word stays balanced — soft consonant, soft vowel.
</p>
<ul class="note-pairs">
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
муж
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
муж
<span class="lit">
ем
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
нож
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
нож
<span class="lit">
ем
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
месец
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
месец
<span class="lit">
ем
</span>
</span>
</li>
</ul>
</article>
### popover [data-note-trigger]|[["data-case-idx","6"],["data-note-id","sib-i"],["data-note-trigger",null]]

</i>

<i lang="sr">

</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
књи
<span class="lit">
зи
</span>
</span>
</li>
<li>
<span class="from" lang="sr">
Амери
<span class="lit">
ка
</span>
</span>
<span aria-hidden="true" class="arrow">
→
</span>
<span class="to" lang="sr">
Амери
<span class="lit">
ци
</span>
</span>
